RealX Product Map

Every user type, journey, screen, action and compliance gate for RealX, an Australian marketplace where sponsors list fractional property trusts, plus the owner's admin panel. Laid out and styled after BrickX, Australia's longest-running retail fractional-property platform.

Overview

How RealX works

Sponsors, who already run property trusts, list them on RealX. Investors buy tokens that are units in those trusts. The trustee's unit register stays the legal record; an ERC-3643 token mirrors it and enforces the rules at every transfer. RealX runs the marketplace, the checks and the money flows, and vets every sponsor.

Investors

Wholesale now, retail from 2027. Verify once, buy tokens, receive monthly income, vote, and resell on a guarded board.

Sponsors

List their trusts, run offers, report monthly on each property, and pay distributions through RealX.

RealX

Marketplace, checks, money movement and the admin panel. Arranges deals as a CAR of an AFSL holder; never owns the properties.

Trustee or RE, custodian, registry

Issue units, hold title and keep the legal register. Retail runs through one umbrella scheme with a hired RE.

Token layer

ERC-3643 tokens mirror the register and enforce identity, caps, residency and lock-ins at every transfer. Operations are signed by a custody policy quorum.

Money

AUD in client-money trust accounts via PayID on the New Payments Platform (NPP) and PayTo. AUD stablecoins later.

Launch phases

P1 · Now to 2027

Wholesale launch

Sponsors issue units of their own wholesale trusts under their own Australian financial services licence (AFSL). RealX arranges as a corporate authorised representative (CAR) and runs the platform. Investors must pass the wholesale test.

78 screens

P2 · From ~8 Apr 2027

Retail and resale

One umbrella registered managed investment scheme (MIS) run by a hired responsible entity (RE), a sub-fund per sponsor property, a product disclosure statement (PDS) and a target market determination (TMD) per listing, timed to the Digital Assets Framework Act. The guarded resale board and on-platform votes switch on once counsel or ASIC relief allows.

9 screens

P3 · Needs a licence, partner or advice sign-off

Later

A continuous licensed market, AUD stablecoin settlement, Auto Invest, guardian accounts for minors, development and debt trusts.

1 screens

Decisions this map is built on

Decided
  • Home base: Australia (founder decision D01, 23 Sep 2026).
  • Model: a marketplace for other sponsors' property trusts; RealX doesn't own properties (D02).
  • Property types: residential and commercial (D03).
  • Defaults assumed from the research pack (P01–P09): licences rented first; the trustee's register is the legal record; non-custodial wallets; AUD first, stablecoins later; no utility token; sponsors carry property operations; audited figures only; plan around the Digital Assets Framework Act; staged resale.
  • Still open: build or buy the token layer.
Open design questions
  • Build or buy the token layer (founder question 12): open standards plus rented services, a white-label vendor, or Tokeniser.
  • Sponsor signing share: does a sponsor hold any custody or signing share, such as a key in the token-agent quorum? The pack leaves this open.
  • Wallet recovery: which mechanism the passkey wallet uses (RealX as guardian, passkey sync or delegate key-sharing). The pack lists options but doesn't choose; token recovery by the agent is the fallback.
  • Sponsor as trustee and tenant admin: on the wholesale track, one sponsor can be both, so some approvals must stay with RealX or the licensee.
  • Retail cooling-off and the s601ED member trigger: questions for counsel (see Compliance).

Maker-checker policy

Every privileged action follows one lifecycle: draft → submitted → prechecked (simulation, canTransfer) → approved → queued for custody → signed by quorum → broadcast → confirmed → reconciled. The approval ID is written into the custody transaction, and the policy engine refuses any call without one. Codes: 4E = a maker and a different checker; 4E+Q = plus custody quorum signing; 6E = a maker and two checkers from different functions; SGL+R = one authorised person acts at once, ratified afterwards; AUTO = the system acts on a rule.

Segregation of duties and break-glass
  • The maker can never be the checker on the same request.
  • AI agents can prepare work but can never check or sign.
  • The platform super-admin never also holds treasury, fund accounting, CFO, token operations or any custody signer role.
  • Whoever initiates a custody transaction can't co-sign it.
  • The distribution maker (FINA) and checker (CFO) are exclusive roles; so are the valuation officer and market operations.
  • A register adjustment by the registrar officer needs CCO + CFO to close the break.
  • The asset manager can propose a sale but can't certify the vote.
  • AML case content is hidden from support and investor relations (no tipping-off).
  • No one grants roles to themselves; engineering can't approve its own upgrade; the offering team can't approve its own compliance review.
  • Break-glass: sealed credentials held by CCO, SECO and the CEO; any 2 of 3 activate; sessions last at most 4 h, are recorded and trigger a board notice and a review within 5 business days.
Key and signer hierarchy
  • V1 Owner: appoints agents, sets compliance and upgrades. Cold MPC or Safe multisig, 3-of-5 (CEO, CFO, CCO, SECO, an independent). 24–72 h timelock; never moves value.
  • V2 Token agent: mint, burn, forced transfer, recovery, partial freeze. Warm MPC, 2-of-3; destination must be identity-registered; needs an approval ID; supply limits.
  • V3 Pauser/freezer: pause and freeze only, 1-of-N (CCO, SECO, MLRO, on-call). Can only restrict; unpausing goes through V2.
  • V4 Identity agent: registerIdentity, updateCountry, deleteIdentity. Service account that auto-signs within policy for approved cases only.
  • V7 Paymaster: gas sponsorship for investors' wallets, auto within a daily cap, with runway alerts.
  • Later: V5 distribution and V6 treasury vaults for AUD stablecoins. Not needed: V8 DeFi admin.
  • Policy engine: approval-ID binding, function allow-lists, supply and destination guards, business-hours window, initiator ≠ approver, 3-of-5 for any policy change.
  • Rotation: hot keys every 90 days, warm keys every 12 months or on staff change; ceremonies witnessed by SECO and the custodian.

Compliance

The gates every action passes

Australian rules decide who may buy, hold and sell. RealX enforces them in three places at once: in the app before an action, in the token's compliance modules at every transfer, and in the admin panel's approvals and monitoring.

IDGateRuleBasisEnforced inLabel
G01Identity verifiedElectronic identity verification (name, date of birth, address) against government sources via the Document Verification Service (DVS), with document and liveness fallback. No action that moves money or tokens before it passes.Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CTF) Act 2006 customer identification; AUSTRAC. BrickX uses Equifax ID Matrix [C]ONB-03 · M07 Onboarding review · identity registry claim checked by ERC-3643 isVerified()C
G02Sanctions and PEP clearScreen people, entities and wallet addresses against the DFAT consolidated list and politically exposed person (PEP) lists at onboarding, on every list update and before each payout or withdrawal.Autonomous Sanctions Act 2011; AML/CTF Act [C/I]ONB-03 · ONB-04 · M20 AML cases · M08 wallet screeningI
G03Entity and owners verifiedFor SMSFs, companies and trusts: verify the entity (ABN/ACN; the know-your-business or KYB check), trustees, directors and every beneficial owner at 25% or more.AML/CTF customer due diligence; beneficial-owner rules [I]ONB-04 · M07I
G04Wholesale status validWholesale track: invest at least A$500k in the offer, or hold an accountant's certificate for net assets of A$2.5m or gross income of A$250k in each of the last two years (valid 2 years), or qualify as sophisticated or professional. Expiry blocks new purchases, not holdings.Corporations Act s761G, s761GA, s708 [I]; thresholds unchanged as of 2026 [C]ONB-06 · INV-01 · M07 · wholesale claim on the investor's identityI
G05Target market fitRetail track: each listing has a TMD. The investor answers the target-market questions; out-of-market applications are stopped or flagged, and significant dealings outside the TMD are reported to the issuer within 10 business days.Design and distribution obligations (DDO), Corporations Act Pt 7.8A [I]ONB-07 · INV-01 · M04 · M19I
G06Residency and FIRBForeign persons cannot buy into established residential dwellings until 30 Jun 2029 (exceptions include build-to-rent, student and aged-care housing, and redevelopments adding 20+ dwellings). Commercial listings may need Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) approval above thresholds. How this applies to fractional units is a counsel question.FATA 1975; FIRB Guidance Note 6 v5 [C]; fractional treatment not addressed [C]M10 rules engine · country and residency rule in the token's compliance module · INV-01C
G07Holder capNo holder (with associates) may exceed the listing's cap. Default 5% per trust, like BrickX, which keeps holders below landholder-duty thresholds (e.g., 20% of a private unit trust in NSW). Checked on every buy and every transfer.State landholder duty [I]; BrickX 5% cap [C]M10 · ERC-3643 max-balance compliance module · INV-01 · INV-06I
G08Lock-in periodTokens bought in a primary offer cannot be listed for resale until the listing's lock-in ends (proposed 3 months, like PRYPCO; set per listing).Pack guard-rail pattern (PRYPCO 3-month lock-in) [C]; RealX default is proposedM10 · time-based transfer rule · INV-05P
G09Price bandResale asks and bids must sit inside a band around the latest independent valuation; RealX's proposed default is ±15% (85% to 115%), set per listing. BrickX's PDS set a floor at 80% of valuation; its live listings on 23 Sep 2026 cluster about 35% below valuation, suggesting a lower floor today.BrickX PDS [C]; live listings observed 23 Sep 2026 [I]; PRYPCO ±15% band [C]M14 resale board · INV-05 · INV-06I
G10Trading haltResale for a trust halts during meetings, around significant events, when a valuation is stale or when reconciliation breaks. Halts are time-boxed with published reasons.BrickX halts trading during meetings [C]M14 · token pause() for the trust · GOV-02C
G11Offer caps and escrowSubscriptions sit in a trust (escrow) account until the soft cap is reached and the offer closes; below the soft cap every investor is refunded in full; oversubscriptions are scaled back to the hard cap.Brickken escrow, soft/hard caps and automatic refunds [C]; Domoblock all-or-nothing [C]INV-01 · INV-03 · SPN-07 · M04 · M05 · M16C
G12Disclosure acknowledgedBefore paying, the investor opens and acknowledges the information memorandum (wholesale) or PDS (retail), the TMD and the fee summary. RealX shows that MIS interests have no cooling-off right.PDS obligations Pt 7.9 [I]; BrickX: no cooling-off rights [C]INV-02 · M18 documentsI
G13Maker-checkerTwo different people approve every money movement above threshold, every mint, burn, freeze, forced transfer or recovery, every valuation and every distribution. The approval ID travels to the custody signer, where a policy quorum signs.Pack design principle: approve in the admin panel, sign in custody. The pack's admin spec is extrapolation, so this is inferred, not confirmed [I]M25 approvals inbox · custody policy engine · SPN-14I
G14AML monitoring and reportsTransaction monitoring rules raise alerts; alerts become cases; suspicious matters are reported to AUSTRAC (SMR), cash over A$10k (TTR) and international transfers (IFTI) are reported; accounts can be frozen with dual control.AML/CTF Act; tranche 2 from 1 Jul 2026 [C]M20 AML cases · M19 filingsC
G15Travel ruleWhen AUD stablecoins go live, originator and beneficiary data travel with every transfer between providers; unhosted wallets get extra checks.AML/CTF reforms for virtual-asset transfers [I]M08 · M20 (P3)I
G16Tax detailsCollect TFN or ABN (otherwise withhold at 47%), tax residency and FATCA/CRS self-certification; withhold managed investment trust (MIT) tax for foreign residents; issue AMMA statements (the annual member statement of an attribution managed investment trust).Tax Administration Act; AMIT regime [I]ONB-05 · POR-07 · M13I
G17Marketing claims approvedEvery public claim goes through a claims library and approval: no 'guaranteed', 'capital protected' or 'backed by real estate' language; yields shown with basis and date.ASIC RG 234 (updated 9 Jun 2026) [C]; Texas SSB order against E-Estate [C]M21 communicationsC

G19Proof of property currentEach trust keeps current evidence of title, council rates and land tax paid, insurance, compliance certificates and reserve balance. Sponsors attest monthly; stale or failed items flag the listing and can pause new offers.RealT failure on property operations [C]; RealX differentiator [P]SPN-10 · M22 property operations · PUB-04 proof-of-property panelP
G20Valuation currentAn independent valuation at least every 6 months (BrickX's cadence) sets the token valuation; stale valuations raise an alert and can halt resale.BrickX semi-annual independent valuations [C]SPN-11 · M03 valuationsC
G21Licence perimeterRealX only offers what its authorisations cover: CAR scope now; from 8 Apr 2027 the Digital Assets Framework Act (DAP/TCP) or its low-value exemption (A$10m a year, A$5k per client) is monitored.Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 [C]M27 licence register and feature flags · M19C

Open questions for Australian counsel

  1. Does RealX need a tokenised custody platform (TCP) licence, a digital asset platform (DAP) licence, or neither under the Digital Assets Framework Act?
  2. Does the low-value exemption (A$10m a year, A$5k per client) cover an early launch?
  3. Would launching wholesale before 8 Apr 2027 make RealX an existing operator, with transition to 8 Oct 2027?
  4. What authorisations does RealX need to arrange sponsors' offers, and what is the right CAR scope?
  5. Can a resale board across many sponsors' trusts run without a market licence, or with ASIC relief?
  6. How does the FIRB established-dwelling ban apply to fractional trust units?
  7. Can one hired RE run a registered scheme whose sub-funds are sourced and managed by different sponsors, and what does each sponsor need?
  8. Can the trust deed designate the token ledger as (or alongside) the s169 register?
  9. Retail cooling-off: none (as in BrickX's PDS) or 14 days (the research pack's inference for retail schemes)?
  10. How does the 20-member registration trigger (s601ED) apply to each sponsor's wholesale trust?
Lifecycles

State machines behind the screens

The states each record moves through, who moves it and what guards each move. Chips on screens and in the admin panel use these state names.

SM-00 Privileged action (every approval)
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> submitted : maker submits
    submitted --> prechecked : simulation and canTransfer
    prechecked --> approved : checkers approve
    approved --> queued_for_custody
    queued_for_custody --> signed : custody quorum
    signed --> broadcast
    broadcast --> confirmed : blocks or registry ack
    confirmed --> reconciled
    reconciled --> closed
    submitted --> rejected : checker rejects
    prechecked --> rejected : precheck fails
    approved --> expired : TTL 72h
    draft --> cancelled : maker cancels
    broadcast --> failed : revert or registry reject
The approval ID travels in the custody transaction note; the policy engine refuses anything without one. A confirmed transaction that the register doesn't reflect is a reconciliation break, not a success.
SM-01 Onboarding case
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> started
    started --> docs_submitted
    docs_submitted --> provider_checks
    provider_checks --> auto_approved : pass and low risk
    provider_checks --> manual_review : refer or hit
    provider_checks --> auto_rejected : fraud signal
    manual_review --> rfi_pending : KYCA asks
    rfi_pending --> docs_submitted : investor replies
    rfi_pending --> expired : 30 days
    manual_review --> edd_review : PEP or high risk
    edd_review --> approved : MLRO and senior manager
    edd_review --> rejected : MLRO
    manual_review --> approved : KYCA
    manual_review --> rejected : KYCA
    auto_approved --> approved : QA sample
    approved --> whitelisted : registerIdentity
    whitelisted --> refresh_due : periodic review
    refresh_due --> whitelisted : refreshed
    refresh_due --> suspended : not refreshed
    whitelisted --> suspended : AML restriction
    suspended --> whitelisted : MLRO then CCO
    suspended --> offboarded
No deposits or purchases before 'whitelisted'. Identity SLA 24 hours. SMSF, trust and company investors add KYB and beneficial-owner steps; the FIRB flag is captured at 'started'.
SM-02 Wholesale certificate
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> requested
    requested --> evidence_submitted
    evidence_submitted --> under_review
    under_review --> rfi : insufficient evidence
    rfi --> evidence_submitted
    under_review --> valid : CLSR issues claim
    under_review --> rejected : CLSR
    valid --> expiring : 30 days before expiry
    expiring --> valid : renewed
    expiring --> expired : two years reached
    valid --> revoked : misrepresentation
    expired --> requested : re-applies
Expiry removes the on-chain wholesale claim: existing holdings stay and can be sold; new wholesale-only purchases are blocked. The A$500k-in-this-offer path is checked by the CCO.
SM-03 Property and listing
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> sourced : sponsor submits
    sourced --> screening
    screening --> rejected : fails criteria
    screening --> due_diligence
    due_diligence --> ic_review
    ic_review --> rejected
    ic_review --> ic_approved : 2 of CFO CCO CEO
    ic_approved --> title_verification
    title_verification --> title_verified
    title_verification --> rejected : title defect
    title_verified --> spv_formed : trust or sub-fund linked
    spv_formed --> listed : offer live
    listed --> funded : offer finalised
    listed --> withdrawn : offer failed
    funded --> operating : tokens minted
    operating --> distressed : arrears or rates overdue
    distressed --> operating : remediated
    distressed --> legal_hold : court order
    legal_hold --> operating : order discharged
    legal_hold --> exit_approved : court-directed sale
    operating --> exit_proposed : vote called
    exit_proposed --> operating : vote failed
    exit_proposed --> exit_approved : vote certified
    exit_approved --> under_sale
    under_sale --> sold
    sold --> wound_down : waterfall paid
Title verification is mandatory (the RealT 'never owned' lesson). Under Torrens title the owner of record is the custodian or trustee. 'Distressed' can halt resale.
SM-04 Offering
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> compliance_review : submit
    compliance_review --> draft : changes requested
    compliance_review --> approved : CCO LEGL and trustee
    compliance_review --> cancelled
    approved --> scheduled
    scheduled --> live : start date
    live --> suspended : pause
    suspended --> live : resume
    live --> soft_cap_reached
    soft_cap_reached --> closed : end date or hard cap
    live --> closed : end date and soft cap missed
    closed --> finalising : allocation locked
    finalising --> minted : CFO and CCO with custody
    closed --> failed : soft cap missed or revert
    failed --> refunding
    refunding --> refunded
A material change during the raise needs investors to re-confirm within 5 business days. Every sponsor offering needs the platform CCO's approval.
SM-05 Order
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> submitted
    submitted --> cancelled : investor cancels
    submitted --> eligibility_check
    eligibility_check --> rejected : KYC wholesale FIRB or cap
    eligibility_check --> reflection_period : retail timer
    eligibility_check --> awaiting_funds : no timer
    reflection_period --> revoked : investor revokes
    reflection_period --> awaiting_funds : timer ends
    awaiting_funds --> funded : payment matched
    awaiting_funds --> expired : funds not received
    funded --> allocated : allocation locked
    funded --> refund_pending : offer failed
    allocated --> settled : tokens delivered
    allocated --> refund_pending : partial allocation
    revoked --> refund_pending : already paid
    refund_pending --> refunded : FINA then CFO
Wholesale orders have no cooling-off timer (BrickX has none either). Whether retail orders get one is a counsel question. 'Settled' means the register entry and the token delivery both exist.
SM-06 Token
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> designed
    designed --> sandbox_deployed : ENGO
    sandbox_deployed --> deploy_requested : tests and audit attached
    deploy_requested --> deployed : owner quorum 3 of 5
    deployed --> configured : registry modules agents
    configured --> issuing : first mint
    issuing --> active : transfers enabled
    active --> paused : pauser then ratified
    paused --> active : CCO then SECO and CFO
    active --> upgrading : 72h timelock
    upgrading --> active
    active --> migrating : critical flaw
    migrating --> retired : holders reissued
    active --> redeeming : exit or wind-down
    redeeming --> retired : supply burned
Compliance modules on every RealX token: country and residency, maximum balance (holder cap), lock-up, and the identity registry. Forced transfers are blocked while a token is paused unless an override is approved.
SM-07 Holding (wallet × token)
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> eligible_empty : identity registered
    eligible_empty --> active : tokens received
    active --> locked : lock-up applied
    locked --> active : lock-in date passed
    active --> partially_frozen : listed for sale or legal
    partially_frozen --> active : unfrozen
    active --> frozen : sanctions or court
    partially_frozen --> frozen
    frozen --> active : MLRO then CCO
    frozen --> recovered_out : recovery or forced transfer
    active --> recovered_out
    active --> eligible_empty : balance zero
    eligible_empty --> deregistered : deleteIdentity
Unfreezing restores rights, so it always needs four eyes. Every holding change reconciles to the s169 register.
SM-08 Distribution run
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft : sponsor accountant
    draft --> calculating : income and snapshot locked
    calculating --> calculated
    calculated --> in_review : exceptions handled
    in_review --> draft : CFO rejects
    in_review --> approved : FINA then CFO
    approved --> funding : TRSY then CFO
    funding --> funded
    funded --> executing : file hash matches
    executing --> executed
    executing --> partially_failed
    partially_failed --> retrying
    retrying --> executed
    partially_failed --> manual_payout
    manual_payout --> executed
    executed --> reconciling
    reconciling --> closed : paid equals approved
    reconciling --> partially_failed : mismatch
    draft --> cancelled
The sponsor signs off before RealX review. Large runs (over $1m or a 25% variance) add the CEO. Mirror BrickX: monthly, within 10 business days, with smoothing.
SM-09 Resale order and trade
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> new_order
    new_order --> validating
    validating --> rejected : band lock-in cap or eligibility
    validating --> open
    open --> partially_filled
    partially_filled --> filled
    open --> filled
    open --> cancelled : investor or ops
    open --> suspended : instrument halted
    suspended --> open : halt lifted
    suspended --> cancelled : halt too long
    filled --> settling : cash and token legs
    settling --> settled
    settling --> settlement_failed
    settlement_failed --> settling : retry up to 3
    settlement_failed --> busted : MKTO then CCO
    settled --> registered : s169 register updated
Instrument states: pre-open → open → halted or closed. A move above 10% in an hour halts trading for 30 minutes. BrickX matches on price-time priority with asks no lower than 80% of valuation (PDS).
SM-10 Governance proposal
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> draft
    draft --> filed : proposal or statutory notice
    filed --> withdrawn
    filed --> discussion : notice published
    discussion --> voting : resale halted
    voting --> tallying
    tallying --> quorum_failed
    tallying --> passed : threshold met
    tallying --> failed
    passed --> certified : scrutineer or RE
    certified --> executing
    executing --> executed
    failed --> cooldown
    quorum_failed --> cooldown
Publishing is blocked if a proposal defaults silence to the manager. BrickX thresholds: 75% at any time, 50% at each 5-year anniversary.
SM-11 AML alert to SMR
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> alert_new
    alert_new --> triage : KYCA
    triage --> closed_false_positive : KYCA then MLRO
    triage --> case_open : escalated
    case_open --> investigating : MLRO
    investigating --> rfi_customer : after tipping-off check
    rfi_customer --> investigating
    investigating --> account_restricted : freeze now, ratify later
    account_restricted --> investigating
    investigating --> smr_decision : MLRO review
    smr_decision --> smr_filed : 24h or 3 business days
    smr_decision --> no_file : documented
    smr_filed --> post_filing_monitoring
    post_filing_monitoring --> exit_relationship
    post_filing_monitoring --> case_closed
    no_file --> case_closed
    exit_relationship --> case_closed
Case access is limited to the MLRO and CCO. Support sees only 'account under review'.
SM-12 Complaint
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> received
    received --> acknowledged : within SLA
    acknowledged --> investigating
    investigating --> redress_proposed
    redress_proposed --> response_issued : CMPH then CCO
    investigating --> response_issued : no redress
    response_issued --> resolved : accepted
    response_issued --> escalated_external : AFCA
    escalated_external --> resolved : outcome implemented
    resolved --> reopened : new information
    reopened --> investigating
    resolved --> closed : retention starts
Any ticket that expresses dissatisfaction converts to a complaint. Redress above $5k adds the CFO. The pack gives no Australian IDR deadlines; set them with counsel.
SM-13 Wallet recovery or forced transfer
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> requested
    requested --> triage : SUPP
    triage --> identity_reverification : lost wallet or estate
    triage --> legal_review : court order or error
    identity_reverification --> legal_review : passes
    identity_reverification --> rejected : fails
    legal_review --> rejected : insufficient evidence
    legal_review --> compliance_approval : evidence complete
    compliance_approval --> checker_approval : CCO
    checker_approval --> old_wallet_frozen : CFO and trustee
    checker_approval --> executing : court order waives timelock
    old_wallet_frozen --> timelock : 48h notice
    timelock --> disputed : holder objects
    disputed --> legal_review
    timelock --> executing : custody 2 of 3
    executing --> confirmed
    confirmed --> register_updated
    register_updated --> closed
Smart-wallet recovery comes first; this is the token-level fallback. The s169 register entry is the legal settlement.
BrickX parity

What BrickX does, and what RealX does instead

BrickX is the Australian baseline: a registered scheme with one trust per property, monthly distributions and an order book. RealX matches it feature for feature, adapted to a marketplace of sponsors, and adds the pieces BrickX lacks.

Only on RealX

Proof of property

Per-property evidence of title, rates and land tax paid, insurance, compliance certificates and reserves, refreshed monthly. Answers the RealT failure.

Sponsor track record

Every sponsor's planned vs actual returns, published and audited. Sponsors keep a stake in each property.

Verifiable register

The trustee's register is mirrored on-chain and reconciled daily with the bank; a public transparency page shows capital raised (not 'tokenised value').

Wallets without seed phrases

Passkey wallets with guardian recovery; the investor holds the tokens.

One KYC, every sponsor

Investors verify once and can invest with any sponsor on the platform.

Faster payouts later

AUD stablecoin distributions once allowed (P3).
